question.text: Ms. Shalini Bhatt, a resident LP, has from AIF pass-through in FY25: INR 20 lakh STCL (short-term capital loss), INR 30 lakh LTCG (long-term capital gain) and INR 8 lakh interest income. Under ITA Sections 70/71/74, how should she set off?

answer.text: STCL can be set off against LTCG AND STCG; therefore set off INR 20 lakh STCL against LTCG — net taxable LTCG INR 10 lakh. Interest INR 8 lakh fully taxable.
STCL can only be set off against STCG (same head and sub-head); so STCL of INR 20 lakh carries forward 8 years; LTCG INR 30 lakh fully taxable.
STCL can be set off against interest income under inter-head rules.
Capital losses of any kind can be set off against any head of income.

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 70: STCL can be set off against both STCG and LTCG (more flexible). But LTCL can ONLY be set off against LTCG. Inter-head (Section 71): capital LOSSES cannot be set off against any other head of income (salary/interest/business). So Shalini's STCL INR 20 lakh offsets the LTCG INR 30 lakh = taxable LTCG INR 10 lakh at 12.5%. Interest INR 8 lakh taxed separately at her slab. The Trap: Option B wrongly restricts STCL to same-head (that rule applies to LTCL). Option C wrongly allows inter-head set-off of capital loss. Option D is a sweeping misstatement. Cross-Exam Context: X-A/B Investment Advisor heavily tests set-off; XIX-C tests this for pass-through reporting accuracy. Manager's Pro-Tip: Design Form 64C so that LPs can see STCL/LTCL/STCG/LTCG and business-income items on separate lines. Many LPs wrongly net losses at fund level — but set-off is a TAXPAYER-LEVEL computation, not a fund-level one.
